\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Build --- Emit Iter Body: Results}

\begin{definition}[States for a machine body]
\lean{Turing.BodyState}
\label{Turing.BodyState}
\leanok
Given two types of states, the body-state type has distinguished states for copying,
rewriting the tape, handling the input tape at its initial position, rewriting the input
tape, anchoring, and starting the second machine. It also has states for calling the
first machine, each carrying one of its states, and for calling the second machine, each
carrying one of its states.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean machine for an iteration body]
\lean{Turing.emitIterBody}
\label{Turing.emitIterBody}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.BodyState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.padAction}
Let $E$ and $G$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, with $k_E$ and
$k_G$ work tapes, and assume $k_E>0$. Choose states $e_e,e_x$ of $E$ and $g_e,g_x$ of
$G$. The constructed machine has $\max(k_E,k_G)$ work tapes and a state set that
includes copying, rewind, input-return, anchoring, and the states used to simulate $E$
and $G$. It copies the input symbols onto work tape $0$, rewinds that tape to its first
blank cell, moves the input head back to its left blank cell, then simulates $E$ from
$e_e$ at the anchor; on reaching $e_x$ it starts $G$ from $g_e$, and on reaching $g_x$
it returns to the anchor. Each simulation uses the corresponding machine's work tapes,
with extra tapes stationary, and returns to its call state unless its current state is
the designated exit state.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Control-only transition]
\lean{Turing.control_step}
\label{Turing.control_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with state set $B$,
and let $q,r\in B$. Suppose that in state $q$, for every input symbol and every tuple of
work-tape symbols, the transition of $H$ moves the input head by zero, leaves all work
tapes and their heads unchanged, emits no output, and enters state $r$. Then for every
configuration $c$ on any Boolean input whose state is $q$, one step of $H$ is the
configuration obtained from $c$ by changing its state to $r$ and leaving all other
components unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Control transition with input movement]
\lean{Turing.control_step'}
\label{Turing.control_step'}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos}
\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with state set $B$,
and let $q,r\in B$ and $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Suppose that in state $q$, for every input
symbol and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the transition of $H$ moves the input head
by $m$, leaves all work tapes and their heads unchanged, emits no output, and enters
state $r$. Then for every configuration $c$ on any Boolean input whose state is $q$, one
step of $H$ is the configuration obtained by setting its state to $r$, moving its input
head by $m$ with boundary clamping, and leaving all its other components unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Embedding a word configuration]
\lean{Turing.embed_ofWords_left}
\label{Turing.embed_ofWords_left}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.embedCfg, Turing.embedCfg_ofWords, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{4}
Fix Boolean machines $E$ and $G$, a Boolean input word $x$, and a state $q$ of $E$. If
$E$ has at least one work tape, then for every Boolean word $s$, embedding the
configuration on input $x$ with state $q$ and with $s$ on tape $0$ (all other tapes
empty) into $\max(k_E,k_G)$ work tapes, using the corresponding left-call state, gives
the configuration on input $x$ with that left-call state and with $s$ on tape $0$ (all
other tapes empty).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Embedding a Right-Call Configuration]
\lean{Turing.embed_ofWords_right}
\label{Turing.embed_ofWords_right}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.embedCfg, Turing.embedCfg_ofWords, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ and $G$ be Boolean machines, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. If $G$ has at
least one work tape, then for every Boolean word $s$ and every state $g$ of $G$,
embedding the configuration with state $g$ and tape words given by the standard word
assignment for $G$ into a machine with $\max(E.k,G.k)$ work tapes, using the right-call
state injection, yields the configuration with the corresponding right-call state and
the same standard word assignment.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One round of the emitted iteration body]
\lean{Turing.body_round}
\label{Turing.body_round}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.BodyState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.control_step, Turing.embedCfg, Turing.embedCfg_output, Turing.embed_ofWords_left, Turing.embed_ofWords_right, Turing.embed_run, Turing.embed_step, Turing.emitIterBody, Turing.padAction, Turing.runFrom_one, Turing.runFrom_output_extends, Turing.runFrom_output_prefix, Turing.stateWord, Turing.state_isSome_of_runFrom}
\difficulty{7}
Let $E$ and $G$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, with states
$e_e,e_x$ for $E$ and $g_e,g_x$ for $G$, and suppose each machine has at least one work
tape. Let $s,e_s,g_s$ be Boolean words. Suppose $E$, started in state $e_e$ with $s$ on
its first work tape and all other work tapes empty, reaches state $e_x$ after $t_E>0$
steps with output $e_s$, and does not enter state $e_x$ at any positive time before
$t_E$. Suppose likewise that $G$, started in state $g_e$ with $s$ on its first work tape
and all other work tapes empty, reaches state $g_x$ after $t_G>0$ steps with first-tape
word $g_s$ and all other work tapes empty, and does not enter state $g_x$ at any
positive time before $t_G$. Then the emitted iteration body, started at its anchor state
with $s$ on work tape $0$ and all other work tapes empty, reaches its
anchor state after $t_E+1+t_G+1$ steps with first-tape word $g_s$, all other work tapes
empty, and output $e_s$; it does not enter the anchor state at any positive time before
then.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Input-copying configuration]
\lean{Turing.copyCfg}
\label{Turing.copyCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.BodyState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
Let $x$ be a Boolean string, let $E$ and $G$ be finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machines,
and choose states $e_e,e_x$ of $E$ and $g_e,g_x$ of $G$. For any $i\le |x|$, the
specified configuration of the iteration-body machine has state $\mathrm{copy}$, input-head
position $i+1$, and empty output. Its work tape $0$ contains the prefix of $x$ of length
$i$, its head is at position $i$, and all other work tapes are blank with their heads at
position $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Specified full configuration]
\lean{Turing.fullCfg}
\label{Turing.fullCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.BodyState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
Let $x$ be a Boolean string, let $E$ and $G$ be finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machines,
and choose states $e_e,e_x$ of $E$ and $g_e,g_x$ of $G$. Given an iteration-body state
$s$, an input-head position $p<|x|+2$, and an integer $z$, the specified configuration
has state $s$, input-head position $p$, and empty output. Work tape $0$ contains all of
$x$ with its head at $z$, while all other work tapes are blank with their heads at $0$.
\end{definition}

Let $E$ and $G$ be finite-state Boolean machines, let $e_0,e_1$ be states of $E$ and
$g_0,g_1$ states of $G$, and suppose $E$ has at least one work tape. For every Boolean
input $x$, the initial configuration of the machine built from these data equals the
copy configuration for the empty copied prefix, with the copying head at position zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[First step of the emission loop]
\lean{Turing.copy_end}
\label{Turing.copy_end}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.inputSymbol_at, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.copyCfg, Turing.emitIterBody, Turing.fullCfg, Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ and $G$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, with $E$ having a
positive number of work tapes, and let $e_e,e_x$ be states of $E$ and $g_e,g_x$ states
of $G$. For any Boolean word $x$, the first step of the emission-loop machine, started
in its copy state with the prefix of length $|x|$ stored on its first work tape and that
tape's head at position $|x|$, is the configuration in its rewind-tape state with input
head at position $|x|+1$ and first work-tape head at position $|x|-1$, with all other
work tapes blank and their heads at zero, and with empty output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rewinding the first work-tape head]
\lean{Turing.rwTape_some}
\label{Turing.rwTape_some}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.emitIterBody, Turing.fullCfg, Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $E$ and $G$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, and suppose $E$ has
at least one work tape. Choose states $e_0,e_f$ of $E$ and $g_0,g_f$ of $G$, and let $x$
be a finite Boolean word. For every integer $j$ with $0\le j<|x|$, the machine
constructed from $E$ and $G$, when in its tape-rewinding state with the input head at
the right boundary blank and the first work-tape head at position $j$, takes one step to
the same state and input-head position, with that work-tape head moved to position
$j-1$; all other tape contents and head positions, as well as the output, are unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Turing.rwTape_none}

Let $E$ and $G$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, with $E$ having
$r>0$ work tapes. Choose states $e_0,e_f$ of $E$ and $g_0,g_f$ of $G$, and let $x$ be a
Boolean word. In the combined machine, if the state is the tape-rewinding state, the
input head is at the right boundary blank cell, the first work-tape head is at position
$-1$, every other work-tape head is at position $0$, the first work tape stores $x$
starting at cell $0$, and all other work tapes are blank, then one step leaves the input
head and all work-tape contents and head positions unchanged, changes the state to the
initial input-rewinding state, and leaves the output empty.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[First Input-Head Rewind Step]

work-tape head at position zero and empty output, yields the configuration with the
input-rewind state, input head at position $|x|$, unchanged work tapes and head

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial run of the emitted iteration body]
\lean{Turing.body_start}
\label{Turing.body_start}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.SafeRun, Turing.SafeRun.cons, Turing.SafeRun.trans, Turing.SafeRun.zero, Turing.copyCfg, Turing.copy_end, Turing.copy_step, Turing.emitIterBody, Turing.fullCfg, Turing.initCfg_eq_copyCfg, Turing.rwIn0_step, Turing.rwInput_some, Turing.rwInput_zero, Turing.rwTape_none, Turing.rwTape_some, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{5}
Let $E$ and $G$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $e_e,e_x$ be
states of $E$, and let $g_e,g_x$ be states of $G$. If $E$ has at least one work tape,
then the emitted iteration body, started on any Boolean input $x$ in its initial
configuration, reaches the anchor state after $3|x|+4$ steps with $x$ on its first work
tape and all remaining work tapes empty. It does not enter the anchor state at any
earlier time, including time zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Iterated emission machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.exists_emitIterTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.exists_emitIterTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_polyBits, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.exists_emitCallTM, Turing.FinTM.exists_emitLoopTM, Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.body_round, Turing.body_start, Turing.emitIterBody, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{7}
Let $G$ and $E$ be finite Turing machines on Boolean words, and let $g,e : \{0,1\}^*
\to \{0,1\}^*$. Suppose there are natural numbers $C_G,c_G,C_E,c_E$ such that $G$
computes $g$ in time $C_G(n+1)^{c_G}$ and $E$ computes $e$ in time $C_E(n+1)^{c_E}$. If
$a',k',b,l$ are natural numbers and every word $w$ and every $i\ge 0$ satisfy
$|g^{i}(w)| \le b(|w|+1)^l$, then there are a finite Turing machine $M$ and natural
numbers $C,c$ such that $M$ computes, in time $C(n+1)^c$, the concatenation of
$e(w),e(g(w)),\ldots,e(g^{a'(|w|+1)^{k'}}(w))$ on input $w$.
\end{theorem}
